### How string escapes work
- The lexer finds the closing quote, then passes the literal's body to `escape::unescape` (`src/lexer/mod.rs:142`).
- `unescape` walks `char_indices()`. Ordinary chars are copied as-is; after a `\` it accepts `n`, `t`, `r`, `0`, `\\`, `\"` and `u{...}` (handed to `read_unicode`).
- Any other char after a backslash returns `LexError::BadEscape { at, found }`; a backslash at the very end returns `LexError::TrailingBackslash { at }`.

So escapes are resolved in a second pass over the literal, not inside the main token loop. Worth keeping that split in the rewrite.
